findings.evidence: template/scripts/model_routing.py:976–982 returns from _require_recovery_safety without postcheck whenever execution is None, except for an open Codex delegation. A Claude delegation that writes only into integration/main leaves task content unchanged; record_claude_execution then fails its postcheck without saving execution. prepare accepts this route at lines 958–961 and captures the already-mutated integration snapshot at line 968. Subsequent containment checks therefore accept the escaped writes as baseline. This contradicts design decision 8 and the delta scenario 'Recovery preserves child safety and outcome', which require unresolved containment violations to block re-routing.
findings.summary: Re-routing can absorb escaped Claude writes into a new containment baseline when no execution receipt exists.

findings.evidence: template/scripts/model_routing.py:1029 preserves only provider, outcome and delegation timestamps in rerouted_from. prepare constructs a fresh Route at line 968 without the previous execution, participant, model, execution identifier or escalation evidence. Once the retry or retained execution completes, _persist_completed_execution overwrites the durable record with this reduced history. The accepted openspec/specs/model-routing/spec.md requirement 'Model routing preserves truthful bounded execution provenance' requires preserving provenance sufficient to distinguish any delegated executor that actually ran; the permitted failed-child re-route loses that information.
findings.summary: An allowed retry after failed Codex execution discards the actual child’s execution provenance.
